vision: Build an open-source, AI-native C++20 + Lua AAA open-world game engine that rivals and surpasses modern AAA engines (like RAGE / GTA VI) while continuously learning from every release, render inspection, and hardware telemetry run.

verifiedEngineeringLessons.lesson: Eliminate road/terrain Z-fighting by sinking buried collision slabs (visible=false), setting camera nearPlane >= 0.50m, layering road elevations cleanly, and sinking flat terrain grid cells 0.22m below flat road planes while skipping completely flat terrain quads.

CPU physics and GPU shaders must share exact analytical formulas: world.sampleWater() evaluates the exact same 4-wave displacement equation as kWaterVertexShader, and Jolt HeightFieldShape leaves water volumes as cNoCollisionValue so dynamic props sink cleanly to the seabed and float via Archimedes buoyancy.

Blender glTF 2.0 export evaluates the top-most (last created) NLA track as the resting bind pose. Always record the upright 'Idle' clip LAST and explicitly keyframe Hips location + rotation in every clip so horizontal poses like 'Swim' never bleed into standing poses.

Avoid Blender Metaballs for procedural characters (MetaElement capsule scale/quaternion quirks cause unpredictable spikes) and avoid loose disconnected tubes. Use clean manifold quad-topology Subdivision-Surface sculpting (bmesh anatomical lofting with seamless armhole/pelvis bridges), polar-aligned eyeballs recessed cleanly behind the brow, true linear PBR colors (sRGB^2.2), and visually verify multi-angle Cycles renders (front 3/4, head close-up, head side profile, walk & run poses) before exporting.

Always align Armature bone rolls predictably (align_roll((0,-1,0)) for limbs) and verify Foot bone dorsiflexion (+X toes up on heel-strike) vs plantarflexion (-X toes down on toe-off). Use periodic Catmull-Rom 8-phase gait curves with lateral hip weight-shift, pelvis/chest counter-rotation, and real-time bone-level TRS/quaternion slerp crossfade blending in C++ so transitions never snap.

Combine procedural FBM rolling hills & surrounding mountain ranges with an analytical road/plaza/lagoon flattening mask, auto-ground off-road scene models in SceneLoader so zero trees/buildings clip or float, mirror the heightmap into a Jolt HeightFieldShape, and sample 4 wheel contact points (FL/FR/RL/RR) for realistic AAA vehicle pitch, roll, and spring-damper suspension.

Pre-warming all .glb models, terrain, and GPU foliage buffers before Frame 1 plus 6-plane Gribb-Hartmann camera frustum culling slashed RTX 5050 cold-start avgFrameMs by 42.1% (49.8ms -> 28.8ms) even while adding 57,290 wind-swaying 3D grass blades (1 glDrawArraysInstanced call with player/vehicle parting) and zero-extra-RT 12-step Screen-Space Reflections packed into RGBA16F FragColor.a.

verifiedEngineeringLessons.domain: GPU Prop Instancing, 3-CSM Shadow LOD & Active Ragdolls
verifiedEngineeringLessons.lesson: When expanding to 3-Split Cascaded Shadow Maps (255m mountain range), always tier Mid/Far cascades to 1024px, compute exact per-model bounding spheres on .glb load, and apply world-radius shadow LOD culling (skipping small props & distant skinned characters in the far cascade). Telemetry caught a 45.0ms draft regression and this fix immediately cut avgFrameMs by 33.8% (to 29.8ms), hit a record-low 179.4ms peak via 1x1 shader warmup, culled 52.8% of entities, and saved 3,315 draw calls/frame via glDrawElementsInstanced prop batching.

verifiedEngineeringLessons.domain: Meshy AI 3D Asset Rigging & Quadruped Animation (Blender 5.3)
verifiedEngineeringLessons.lesson: Raw Meshy .glb exports often fail Blender Bone Heat Weighting due to overlapping accessories (backpacks/belt pouches) and micro-doubles, or include stray wrapper meshes (Icosphere) and huge 4K textures (50MB+). For humanoids, weld micro-doubles and use anatomical region-masked capsule skinning + 3x Laplacian joint smoothing + 4-weight clamping so backpacks and pouches stay rock-solid while limbs bend cleanly. For pre-rigged quadrupeds (like Meshy's 56-bone Wolf), preserve existing skin weights, downscale 4K textures to 1024px (~9x smaller GLB), remove stray meshes, and animate bones via world-space-to-bone-local quaternion transforms (R_local = R_rest_inv @ R_world @ R_rest) so animations work cleanly regardless of arbitrary bone roll orientations.

verifiedEngineeringLessons.domain: Double-Sided PBR Normals, Depth Water, Entity-Space Look-At IK & Release Optimization
verifiedEngineeringLessons.lesson: Never run bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals on open-card Meshy cloth/fur meshes — it flips single-sided cards inward, and without 'if (!gl_FrontFacing) N = -N;' in kLitFragmentShader back-faces evaluate dot(N,V)<=0 causing 100% white Fresnel mirror speckles. For multi-bone quadruped Look-At IK (e.g. 5-neck-bone Wolf), divide role share by exact head/neck/chest counts and transform entity-space yaw/pitch into bone-local space via conjugate(restWorldRot) * qEntity * restWorldRot. Copy opaque HDR depth via glCopyTexSubImage2D before Pass 3 so water computes exact per-pixel depth for soft beach fade & surf foam with zero harsh seams. Merging identical-material static .glb submeshes on load + zero-allocation per-frame skeletal pose caching + time-sliced Far 3-CSM + Release (/O2) build cut Stunt City draw calls by 40.7% (1,932 -> 1,145) and session time by 34.6% (0.945s -> 0.618s) while Echo Island Survival runs at 147 draw calls with 216,000 shadowed grass blades.

verifiedEngineeringLessons.domain: Benchmark Methodology, Simulation Clock & Lua Sandbox
verifiedEngineeringLessons.lesson: A 12-frame --smoke-test average is NOT a performance number: one 200-250 ms cold-start frame dominates it, and the old telemetry clamped frame times to the 250 ms simulation cap, so every hitch read as exactly 250 ms. On the same Release build and RTX 5050 Laptop GPU, the 12-frame average read 20-26 ms but steady state was p50 2.3-2.4 ms (Stunt City) and 1.9-2.6 ms (Echo Island) via --benchmark (120 warm-up + 600 measured frames, VSync off). Earlier logged 'speedups' were within that cold-start noise, so re-baseline from --benchmark p50/p95/p99, run twice, and treat differences inside the run-to-run spread (about 10-25% here) as noise. Separately, physics/water/sage.getTime() used wall-clock time, so catch-up fixed ticks in one frame all saw the same time (getTime-driven objects stalled, buoyancy drifted from the rendered waves). Advance a simulation clock by exactly dt per fixedTick and render shaders at simTime + accumulator. Finally, Lua base-lib dofile/loadfile and binary load() escape the sandbox, and an infinite loop froze the engine. Remove them and arm a LUA_MASKCOUNT watchdog hook per host->Lua call so runaway scripts error out and pause only their own resource.

With a fixed 60 Hz simulation and VSync off, SAGE drew ~7 frames per tick (419 UI frames over 62 ticks), so un-interpolated motion repeated each snapshot and then jumped (judder at any refresh rate above 60 Hz). Capture a per-entity/light/camera snapshot at the start of each fixedTick, draw prev + (cur - prev) * (accumulator / dt), and restore the true state before the editor and Lua UI run. Blend Euler yaw along the shortest arc, quaternions via shortest-hemisphere nlerp, and animation clocks forward-only. Snap on spawn, on world.teleport()/camera.cut(), and on any move over 25 m per tick. Leave unchanged values bit-identical so static-prop caches are unaffected. Measured cost: none (p50 2.35-2.39 ms on vs 2.36-2.40 ms off, Release, RTX 5050 Laptop).

Game-specific landscapes hard-coded in engine C++ (coordinates of peaks, lakes, ring roads; grass exclusions tied to those roads) force C++ edits for every new game. Move them into a scene JSON spec evaluated by ONE function (baseHeight + heightmap + FBM -> island mask -> ordered peak/basin/flatten/road features) that the GPU mesh, Jolt HeightField, grass scatter and Lua sampleTerrain all share. Gate renderer/physics rebuilds on a revision counter bumped on every scene load, not on a few cached numbers (the old cache missed hot-reloaded terrain edits). Validate every key with file + JSON-path errors, warn on unknown keys (catches typos) and on 0..255 colours, and fall back to flat terrain on errors. Keep legacy presets byte-identical and prove it: same triangle/grass/collider counts and ~0.1% pixel diff (moving objects only) between old and new builds from identical cameras. Gotcha: culling seabed triangles near the water surface (hideBelowHeight) causes a stair-step seam because the water shader shades by depth.

With many resources in one Lua state, a single global sage.saveData writing saves/<key>.dat lets mods overwrite each other's saves. Give each resource its own `sage` table (metatable __index -> the shared table) whose save functions are bound to saves/<resource folder>/, so isolation needs no API change. Write to <key>.dat.tmp then rename over the target so a crash never leaves a half-written save. Migrate legacy saves/<key>.dat lazily on first load and rename it to .migrated so no other resource can claim it. Also re-migrate when the legacy file is NEWER than the per-resource copy: a player may still be running an older build that keeps saving to the old path, and preferring the stale migrated copy would silently lose progress. Test saves in an isolated project copy (junction the assets folder) so test runs never touch the user's real saves.
